name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Babin running with a large cash advantage
Democrat Rhonda Hart has raised no money
Prediction markets price Republican win around 93%
model.rationale: Babin holds a heavily Republican seat, has roughly $900,000 on hand, and faces a Democratic opponent with no reported fundraising; markets price his reelection near 93%. The forecast stays close to fundamentals, tilted slightly more Republican given the money gap.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending putting the seat in play would be the first sign of a real challenge.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
East Texas's 36th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Brian Babin is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. He enters the general election with about $900,000 in the bank, while Democratic challenger Rhonda Hart reports no fundraising and no cash on hand. No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Babin roughly a 93% chance of winning. With a double-digit Republican district lean, a well-funded incumbent, and an underfunded challenger, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
